items.summary: This is the same consolidated Seventh Circuit opinion in Nos. 25-2461 and 25-2487, filed under the United States of America v. State of Illinois, et al. caption, addressing challenges to Illinois Senate Bill 2930 and its requirement that covered charitable organizations post demographic information about their directors and officers. The court reversed the district court's dismissal of the complaints of the American Alliance for Equal Rights and the United States, vacated the denial of preliminary injunctive relief, and remanded for further proceedings. The court concluded that it could exercise pendent appellate jurisdiction over the standing determinations because the denials of preliminary injunctions rested on those determinations alone; the source text is truncated before the court's discussion of the United States' intervention under 42 U.S.C. § 2000h-2.

items.summary: In a nonprecedential order, the Seventh Circuit affirmed the Central District of Illinois's denial of a third motion for compassionate release under 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c)(1)(A)(i) filed by Timothy B. Fredrickson, a federal prisoner serving 200 months for sexual exploitation of a minor. The court found no abuse of discretion, holding that a single latent tuberculosis diagnosis and general measles statistics did not establish an ongoing outbreak, imminent risk of one, or an ongoing public health emergency at FCI Seagoville under U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(1)(D). The court further noted that, because no extraordinary and compelling reason was shown, the district court was not required to consider the § 3553(a) factors, citing Rutherford v. United States.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Illinois's grant of summary judgment dismissing James Hsieh's claim against PitchBook Data, Inc. under the Illinois Right of Publicity Act (IRPA) as untimely. The court held that a one-year statute of limitations applies to IRPA claims, following its earlier decision in Giovannelli v. Walmart Inc., 164 F.4th 1052 (7th Cir. 2026), and declined Hsieh's request to revisit that holding based on the Act's property-rights designation. The opinion relies on Blair v. Nevada Landing Partnership, 859 N.E.2d 1188 (Ill. App. Ct. 2006), which the court found Illinois courts have continued to follow.

items.summary: In this nonprecedential order, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit affirmed the Southern District of Indiana's denial of Deandre Govan's motion for compassionate release under 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c)(1)(A)(i). The court found the government had forfeited its argument that Govan's notice of appeal was untimely, and it concluded on the merits that the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding no extraordinary and compelling reasons for release and in weighing Govan's violent criminal history and the danger he posed to the community. The order also states that the amended U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13 policy statement governs prisoner-initiated motions, so the district court appropriately followed it.

items.summary: In a consolidated opinion in Nos. 25-2461 and 25-2487, the Seventh Circuit reviewed the district court's rulings on challenges by the American Alliance for Equal Rights and the United States to Illinois Senate Bill 2930, which requires charitable organizations reporting grants of $1,000,000 or more to post aggregated demographic information about their directors and officers on their websites. The court held that it had pendent appellate jurisdiction to review the standing determinations because they were inextricably intertwined with the denial of preliminary injunctions, and it disagreed with the district court's standing analysis. The court reversed the dismissal of both complaints, vacated the denial of injunctive relief, and remanded for further proceedings; the source text is truncated before the court's discussion of the United States' intervention under 42 U.S.C. § 2000h-2.

items.summary: In a nonprecedential order, the Seventh Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Illinois's dismissal of Kimberly Lopez's suit under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 and Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act against 29 defendants involved in her ongoing Cook County child-custody proceedings. The district court had applied the Rooker-Feldman doctrine to some claims, abstained under J.B. v. Woodard, 997 F.3d 714 (7th Cir. 2021), from the remaining claims, and dismissed rather than stayed them. The appellate court held that abstention was appropriate because the federal action sought to affect the ongoing state custody dispute, and that dismissal was warranted because a stay was impractical given the expected length of the state proceedings.

items.summary: In an opinion not recommended for publication filed November 18, 2026, the Sixth Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Ohio's grant of summary judgment to Tenisha Wilson and Denman Gordon on their claim that the City of South Euclid, Ohio abandoned its interest in a strip of 'Laurens Avenue,' a platted but unbuilt street abutting Wilson's property, which reverted to the abutting owners. The court concluded that the City's 1927 acceptance of the Green-Anderson Plat, which locked Laurens Avenue at 25 feet, evinced intent to abandon, and that 21 years of nonuse had run by 1948. The opinion was issued in consolidated appeal Nos. 25-4023/4026, and the court also addressed the cross-appeal on the class-of-one equal protection claim, which the district court had rejected.
items.title: Tenisha Wilson, et al v. City of South Euclid, OH

items.summary: In a nonprecedential opinion (File Name 26a0464n.06, marked not recommended for publication), the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit denied the petition for review by Geraldine Faizuly Doza Castro and her minor child, Colombian citizens who sought asylum, withholding of removal, and Convention Against Torture protection, in a case captioned against Attorney General Todd Blanche. The court held that the petitioner forfeited her challenges to the particularity and social distinctiveness of her proposed social group, 'witness to a crime,' by not developing them before the Board of Immigration Appeals. The court also held that substantial evidence supported the Board's conclusion that Colombian public officials did not acquiesce in torture, citing the family's failure to report the threats to police.

items.summary: In a nonprecedential order, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit granted appointed counsel's motion to withdraw under Anders v. California and dismissed the appeal of Calvin Carter, who pleaded guilty to drug-distribution offenses and was sentenced to 192 months' imprisonment. The court held that Carter's appeal waiver barred review of the pretrial indictment ruling and the sentence, that the plea colloquy complied with Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11, and that challenges to the waiver's enforceability and to the sentence would be frivolous. The order noted that any ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim is best raised on collateral review.

items.summary: In an opinion not recommended for publication filed November 18, 2026, the Sixth Circuit affirmed the Western District of Michigan's grant of summary judgment to the defendants in an action by Lori Viilo, personal representative of the estate of Joshua Maslowski, who died in 2021 while a pretrial detainee at the Kent County Correctional Facility. The court stated that Viilo had not overcome the deputy defendants' qualified immunity defense and had not shown that the medical defendants were deliberately indifferent to Maslowski's serious medical needs. The opinion sets out the factual background, including Maslowski's complaints to staff before he was found unresponsive after an apparent seizure, and identifies the medical examiner's determination that the cause of death was a malignant brain tumor.

items.summary: In an opinion not recommended for publication filed November 18, 2026, the Sixth Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Ohio's judgment sentencing Michael Hollis to 78 months of imprisonment after he pleaded guilty to possessing a firearm as a convicted felon under 18 U.S.C. Section 922(g)(1). Hollis argued that the district court should have sua sponte ordered a competency hearing, that the four-level enhancement for possessing a firearm in connection with another felony should not have applied, and that the sentence was unreasonably long. The court reviewed the competency claim for plain error, found no reversible error in the district court's competency determination, and affirmed the district court in full.

Buesing's motion to proceed in forma pauperis on appeal and dismissed his appeal as frivolous. The court concluded that his challenges to the treatment of a broken arm, including the timing of hospital transport, did not present a nonfrivolous issue under 42 U.S.C. Section 1983. The court stated that the district court's dismissal of his complaint and this appeal each count as a strike under 28 U.S.C. Section 1915(g), giving him two strikes, and warned that a third strike would bar him from proceeding in forma pauperis while incarcerated or detained absent imminent danger of serious physical injury.

items.summary: In a per curiam opinion filed November 18, 2026, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the Southern District of Florida's denial of Isaac Raldy Louiniste's 28 U.S.C. § 2254 habeas petition as untimely. The court held that a petition for a belated appeal under Florida Rule of Appellate Procedure 9.141(c) is an original proceeding that does not toll the one-year limitations period under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(d)(2), and that the petition was filed 18 days after the period expired. The opinion is marked not for publication.

items.summary: In a per curiam opinion filed November 18, 2026, the Eleventh Circuit dismissed for lack of jurisdiction the pro se appeal of defendant Sanjay Singh in a Securities and Exchange Commission civil enforcement action. The court held that the district court's May 21, 2026 summary judgment order on liability was not final, because it did not determine the relief sought and did not resolve the claims against defendant Royal Bengal Logistics, Inc., and was not appealable under the collateral order doctrine.   Mr. MAST. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the bill
(H.R. 5490) to establish an interagency Task Force to dismantle and
shut down transnational criminal syndicates p
items.summary: Representative Mast moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 5490, the "Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act," as amended, and the bill text is reproduced. The bill's findings describe "pig butchering" investment scams and scam compounds in Burma, Laos, and Cambodia, and it directs the President to establish within 30 days an interagency Task Force chaired by the Secretary of State to develop a comprehensive U.S. Government strategy within 240 days and to submit annual reports for five years. The Task Force would terminate five years after enactment, and the text provided is truncated before its final provisions.
items.title: DISMANTLE FOREIGN SCAM SYNDICATES ACT

items.opening_verbatim:
PREVENTIVE HEALTH SAVINGS ACT

  Mr. ARRINGTON. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 4464) to amend the Congressional Budget Act of 1974
respecting the scoring of preventive health savings.
items.summary: H.R. 4464, the "Preventive Health Savings Act," would add a new subsection (h) to section 202 of the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974. Upon request by the designated congressional leaders, the CBO Director would determine whether proposed legislation yields net reductions in budget outlays in budgetary outyears through preventive health care, defined as two consecutive 10-year periods beginning 10 years after the current fiscal year, and any such estimate would be supplementary and not used for budgetary enforcement controls. During floor debate under suspension, Representatives Arrington and Boyle described the bill as allowing analysis beyond the standard 10-year scoring window for health-related savings.
items.title: PREVENTIVE HEALTH SAVINGS ACT

items.opening_verbatim:
{time}  1500
         SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT INFORMATION DATABASE ACT OF 2026

  Mr. PALMER. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 7934) to amend chapter 3 of title 5, United States Cod
items.summary: Representative Palmer moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 7934, the "Settlement Agreement Information Database Act of 2026," which would add section 307 to subchapter I of chapter 3 of title 5, United States Code. The section requires agencies to establish and maintain public online databases of covered settlement agreements within two years of enactment, with covered agreements including those requiring at least $10,000,000 in explicitly obligated payments, those involving a special master or monitor, and those involving a non-Federal government party, subject to listed exemptions. The bill also directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in coordination with the Attorney General, to issue implementing guidance and requires agencies to submit annual reports on covered agreements not publicly disclosed.
items.title: SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT INFORMATION DATABASE ACT OF 2026

items.summary: Senator Durbin, with cosponsors, introduced S. 5767, the Student Loan Borrower Bill of Rights, which was referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and its text was ordered printed in the Record. items.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or “Department”) is issuing this final rule to modify the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information (“Privacy Rule”) under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act. These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.

items.summary: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) is proposing amendments to its executive and director compensation disclosure rules to make the requirements more principles-based and to reduce compliance burdens for registrants, while maintaining the disclosure of material information to investors. items.summary: The Coast Guard will enforce a safety zone for the Magnificent Mile Fireworks Display on November 21, 2026, to provide for the safety of life on navigable waterways during this fireworks display. items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-12-08, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters. AD 2026-12-08 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-12-08, a determination was made that new and more restrictive airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks are necessary. This proposed AD would require incorporating these airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks into the ALS of the existing MM or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) proposes to amend the Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E) regulations to align with current practice and statute. The rule would expand the list of approved providers for reduced work tolerance (RWT) documentation, allowing for more accurate and timely processing by a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor (VRC). VA also proposes to clarify that a veteran who is subject to a basic period of eligibility would receive a new 12-year period of eligibility if such veteran obtains a compensable service-connected disability rating based on a subsequent period of active-duty service. Finally, the rule would remove the eligibility termination date for veterans discharged on or after January 1, 2013, consistent with the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2020.
items.title: Veteran Readiness and Employment Program: Update to Reduced Work Tolerance and Basic Eligibility Period

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3 and EC635T2+ helicopters. items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-14-09, which applies to certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X, FALCON 900EX, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. AD 2024-14-09 requires replacement of certain titanium screws, adds other locations for screw replacement, and revises the applicability from AD 2022-02-10. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-14-09, affected parts have been found in other areas of certain FALCON 7X airplanes as well as in additional FALCON 7X airplanes. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-14-09 and would require expanding the applicability to additional airplanes, expanding the locations for screw replacement, and revising the compliance times for parts replacement. This AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-12-17, which applies to certain ATR—GIE Avions de Transport Régional Model ATR42-300, -320, and -500 airplanes; and all Model ATR72-101, -102, -201, -202, -211, -212, and -212A airplanes. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2025-5401; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01313-A; Amendment 39-23525; AD 2026-24-01] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; General Atomics AeroTec
items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (General Atomics) Model Dornier 228-100, Dornier 228-101, Dornier 228-200, Dornier 228-201, Dornier 228-202, and Dornier 228-212 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of specific part-numbered hydraulic pump motors becoming severely damaged by excessive heat. This AD requires replacing the affected hydraulic pump motor with an improved design hydraulic pump motor. This AD also prohibits installing an affected hydraulic pump motor on any airplane. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (Type Certificate Previously Held by RUAG Aerospace Services GmbH) Airplanes

items.summary: H.R. 9624, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, was introduced in the House on July 9, 2026, by Mr. Crawford, referred to the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and reported with an amendment on November 18, 2026 (Report No. 119–886). The bill would authorize fiscal year 2027 appropriations for intelligence and intelligence-related activities, the Intelligence Community Management Account, and the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System. Its table of contents lists provisions on intelligence community matters, budget and inspectors general, Office of the Director of National Intelligence and Central Intelligence Agency items, Department of Defense and overhead architecture, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Department of Homeland Security, and reports; the provided excerpt is truncated before the full text.
